messages:
maya: Kicked off prod rollout at 09:12 PT. Canary to 1% for 10m, 3 instances per AZ. starting smoke checks

sam: Canary looks reachable — healthchecks 200/200 on initial probes. running a couple of quick requests now:
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

sam: streaming handshake ok, chunked output received, latency ~85ms avg for sample queries

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T16:12:04Z started by maya — canary initiated (id: deploy-1899991111)

kevin: watching metrics — 95p latency ~120ms, cpu/gpu utilization within expected range. no big change in qps

lucy: noticed a small bump in 5xxs from model-worker-2 during the first minute: 5 -> 8 requests (0.5%). keeping an eye. logs show transient kv-cache timeout on a handful of requests

maya: holding canary at 1% while we surface traces. @kevin @sam please check traces for cache timeouts

sam: traces point to a race in cache refresh on model-worker-2, reproducer near prefix-cache miss. I can push a quick patch if we want to proceed

kevin: patch sounds good. if we need rollback readiness: rollback script is /ops/scripts/rollback_latest.sh and we have image tag pinned to release-20260317. Ops oncall can run it in ~2m

maya: go ahead with the patch then. prioritize minimal change (guard + metrics). will pause ramp until canary clear. (thumbsup emoji)

sam: pushed hotfix to model-worker (thread-safety guard around cache refresh). redeploying canary instances now

deploy-bot: Canary redeploy complete for deploy-1899991111 — healthchecks passing across nodes

lucy: post-redeploy metrics: 5xxs back to baseline, latency improved ~10ms on median. CPU stable.

maya: good. increasing canary to 10% for 15m. keep watchlist for error-rate >1% or latency regression >20%

kevin: setting a short-lived alert group: monitor group "postdeploy-1899991111" with thresholds: errors >1% for 5m, p95 latency +20% for 10m

jordan: note for docs: we should add a step in the postdeploy checklist to flush prefix cache when rolling model-worker changes. I'll open a tiny PR against ops-runbook

maya: thanks @jordan — opening handoff: ops/monitoring team owns the 60m watch. If any threshold hits rollback unless the fix mitigates within 10m. closing here, will update the release ticket with canary metrics and action items. :white_check_mark:
